correctness.rationale: At strictly positive equilibria P_i=I_i, R_i=aI_i/b and S_i=1-(1+a/b)I_i. Dividing equilibrium equations by full positive product Q yields common strictly decreasing f(z)/Q(z), forcing equal I_i. Scalar equilibrium F(x) decreases from R0 to zero, so unique iff R0>1. Physical 3n Jacobian diagonalizes via symmetric and zero-sum eigenvalues θ+=1+(n-1)w, θ-=1-w>=0. Verified algebraically independently using SymPy the block M(v), char cubic A1=b+c+u, A2=u(a+b)+c(b+u+v), A3=c(u(a+b)+bv), and A1A2-A3=(b+u)[u(a+b)+c(b+u+c)]+cv(u+c)>0. All finite n modes strictly Hurwitz; no assertion of global stability or uniform rate.
